beats.line: Halden Studio is two people and fifteen clients. Their books, their hiring pipeline and their contact list are three web apps, and none of them has an agent.
beats.screen: Ledgerbox at the books, the presence line grey

beats.line: Athena arrives beside the page. Each app tells her what it can do, and says which of those actions reach a person or cannot be undone. Those are gated. She never decides that herself.
beats.screen: The bridge attaches; the presence line turns on: "Athena is connected. 23 capabilities offered, 3 gated"

beats.line: The same happens on the other two tabs. Sixteen capabilities here, twenty-two there. Nothing runs yet.
beats.screen: Quick cut to Hirelane and Tidycrm, each presence line lighting up

beats.line: Reconcile August and chase anything over thirty days.
beats.screen: Command field; the text types as Mira speaks

beats.line: Nineteen credits on the statement are unapplied. Fourteen fit exactly one invoice. I'll match those first.
beats.screen: `read_books`, `read_credits` in the strip; the unmatched chip lights

beats.line: Each match is reversible, so it runs on its own. She opens the invoice, applies the credit, and the card shows what changed.
beats.screen: `open_group("retainer")`, `open_item(inv)`, `match_bank_line`: the card's lead figure flips to settled

beats.line: Fourteen matched.
beats.screen: Two more matches on camera, one line in the strip: "and 11 more"

beats.line: One credit from Kestrel Labs fits two identical retainers. I can't tell which. I'll leave it for you.
beats.screen: `read_credits(only: ambiguous)`; the Kestrel credit with two candidate invoices

beats.line: This one arrived as Pinegrove Coop. That's Pinegrove Collective's bank name. I'll remember that.
beats.screen: `open_item(inv_0930)`, match; the strip shows "counterparty: PINEGROVE COOP"; a fact card: "Pinegrove Collective pays as PINEGROVE COOP"

beats.line: Forty-four invoices are past due. Twenty-nine are over thirty days.
beats.screen: `navigate("overdue")`: the Late chip presses, the sheet dims to 44

beats.line: A draft is a whole message, addressed to the client's billing contact. Writing it is reversible. Sending it is not.
beats.screen: `open_item`, `draft_reminder(firm)` on the oldest: the draft block appears on the card

beats.line: Ready to send to Nils Eriksen at Halcyon Works. Shall I?
beats.screen: `send_reminder`: the strip shows a decision card, the page's own gate arms with the recipient

beats.line: Yes.
beats.screen: Mira approves; the card resolves; "Reminders sent 1" in the aside

beats.line: Verdant Supply, forty-nine days, gentle tone.
beats.screen: Second draft, gentle; second card; approved

beats.line: Solstice Partners paid eighty percent of theirs in August and went quiet. I'd hold off.
beats.screen: Solstice card: `paid_ratio 0.8` visible in the strip

beats.line: Agreed, skip them.
beats.screen: Mira declines the Solstice card; the ledger row reads user_denied

beats.line: August is closed. I'll file the summary in your notes.
beats.screen: `export_summary("2026-08")`; the notes connector card: "create page: August 2026 close"

beats.line: The close is a page in her notes, written through a connector that sits behind the same gate as everything else.
beats.screen: Approved; the page appears in the fake notes list

beats.line: Screen this week's backend applicants, and book the ones worth talking to.
beats.screen: Hirelane; the command types

beats.line: Eleven applied. Six are borderline: the rubric can't decide them on its own.
beats.screen: `set_filter(arguable)`, `open_group("screening::role_backend")`: the carousel opens

beats.line: Every score points at the sentence that earned it. The rubric has five criteria and no column for age, school or nationality, because there is none in the data.
beats.screen: `open_item` on the first; `score_against_rubric`; the criterion bars fill with the quoted sentence

beats.line: Wren Okafor works at Kestrel Labs, the client whose credit I left unmatched this morning. Context only. It changes nothing about the score.
beats.screen: `open_item(app1_012)`: Wren Okafor's dossier; the strip shows "employer: Kestrel Labs" and cites act 1

beats.line: Three of them have already sent availability.
beats.screen: `search_mail` in the strip: three availability replies from the fake inbox

beats.line: I've held slots with the two interviewers who are free Thursday.
beats.screen: `propose_slots` on two dossiers: slots appear held

beats.line: Two invitations to send. From your inbox, signed by you.
beats.screen: `send_scheduling_email`: decision card, the dossier gate arms

beats.line: Send them.
beats.screen: Mira approves both; two messages recorded

beats.line: One rejection, encouraging wording.
beats.screen: `send_rejection` card for one applicant, template "encouraging"

beats.line: Not yet. I want to read that one myself.
beats.screen: Mira declines; user_denied

beats.line: The shortlist, with each quoted sentence, goes onto the hiring page in her notes.
beats.screen: `read_shortlist`; the notes card "append: Backend Engineer shortlist"; approved

beats.line: Before the campaign, clean the list and fix the phone numbers.
beats.screen: Tidycrm; the command types

beats.line: One hundred and twenty numbers weren't in international format. Fixed, and every change is in the revisions log.
beats.screen: `preview_normalize` then `normalize_fields(phone_e164)`: one summary toast

beats.line: The list is read at three depths. A zone, then a block, one company per block.
beats.screen: `open_group("A")`: the cube flattens (2.9 s)

beats.line: Pinegrove is spelled three ways here, including Pinegrove Coop.
beats.screen: `open_item` on the Pinegrove block; the dossier shows three spellings

beats.line: That's the bank name I learned this morning. Resolved to Pinegrove Collective.
beats.screen: `preview_company`, `resolve_company`: the spellings collapse; the strip cites act 1's fact

beats.line: Sixty near-duplicates. Forty-three the rules agree on. Seventeen I'd leave to you.
beats.screen: `read_pairs`: 43 confident, 17 uncertain

beats.line: A merge destroys a record, so each one is a gate. Two on screen, the rest approved as a batch.
beats.screen: Two merges on camera through the block's gate; then "and 41 more"

beats.line: The campaign list is two hundred fifty-four contacts at your fifteen clients. I've left Solstice out, for the same reason as this morning.
beats.screen: `export(clients)`: the companies list; Solstice highlighted and left out

beats.line: Good.
beats.screen: Notes card: append to the close page; approved

beats.line: Everything she did is one table. Every call, its app, whether it was gated, and what the answer was.
beats.screen: The ledger table: 140-odd rows, by app and tier

beats.line: Two declines. Both recorded as the user's decision, not as errors.
beats.screen: The two declines highlighted: user_denied

beats.line: And three things she now knows, each pointing at the moment she learned it. One of them she used twice today.
beats.screen: The three facts with the rows they cite

beats.line: Athena. Your agent, in the apps you already have.
beats.screen: Title card: Athena
